books.section: Topic 4.9 The Development of an American Culture, A. The Emergence of a National Culture

stimulus.text:
The table lists major works of the American Renaissance, the flowering of American literature in the early 1850s.

| Work | Author | Year |
|---|---|---|
| The Scarlet Letter | Nathaniel Hawthorne | 1850 |
| The House of the Seven Gables | Nathaniel Hawthorne | 1851 |
| Moby-Dick | Herman Melville | 1851 |
| Walden | Henry David Thoreau | 1854 |
| Leaves of Grass | Walt Whitman | 1855 |
stimulus.source_note: Table compiled from Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 6, Topic 4.9 A, which names these five works as the peak of the American Renaissance in the early 1850s. Titles, authors, and years are as given in the book. Original synthesis, not a quotation.

source: original; stimulus as described in the stimulus source note
stem: According to the table, which work appeared first?

options.misconception: Moby-Dick is the most famous title here, so it is easy to pick it first.
Walden is the best-known transcendentalist book, so it is easy to put it first.
Whitman is often named first among American poets, so it is easy to put him first.

rationales.A: Moby-Dick appeared in 1851, one year after The Scarlet Letter.
rationales.B: The table dates The Scarlet Letter to 1850, the earliest year listed.
rationales.C: Walden appeared in 1854, four years after The Scarlet Letter.
rationales.D: Leaves of Grass appeared in 1855, the latest year in the table.
rationales.general:
1. Read the Year column top to bottom: 1850, 1851, 1851, 1854, 1855.
2. Take the smallest year. 1850 belongs to The Scarlet Letter.
3. Check the row. The 1850 row names Hawthorne's The Scarlet Letter.
Background: the table gathers the early-1850s peak of the American Renaissance.
Remember: with a table, read the column the question asks about before you read the names.
